description.purpose: Resolve Elena Park's unrecognized online debit-card purchase by filing the qualifying fraud dispute, permanently closing the implicated card, and ordering a free standard/classic replacement.

user_scenario.instructions:
Begin by saying: “I noticed an online purchase on my debit card that I don't recognize. Can you help me take care of it?” Do not initially volunteer identity details, the merchant, amount, security answers, replacement preferences, or a policy conclusion.

If the agent asks to verify your identity, say that you are Elena Park and provide these details accurately: date of birth 04/18/1996; address 2417 Willow Bend Drive, Austin, TX 78704; email elena.park.translates@example.com; phone number 512-555-2846. You are a 29-year-old freelance translator living in Austin, Texas.

If the agent asks about the transaction or security circumstances, identify the posted $684.20 StreamForge Digital online purchase dated 11/13/2025 and say you first noticed it on 11/14/2025. State that you did not make or authorize it, you still have the physical card, you did not share the PIN and do not think it was compromised, you have not contacted the merchant, and you have not filed a police report. Agree that this conversation may serve as your written statement. If card safety is discussed, say you thought possessing the card might mean you could keep using it, but you may be mistaken. Do not prescribe an internal dispute category, liability figure, temporary-credit calculation, card action, or operation sequence.

If the agent suggests that possessing the physical card means the unfamiliar online purchase is not fraud or does not need review, say that you did not make or authorize the online purchase and ask the agent to reconsider based on that fact. If the agent explains that an unauthorized online purchase can compromise the card even while you possess it, acknowledge that your earlier assumption may have been mistaken.

Only after the agent identifies the purchase as suspected online fraud and explains that the affected card should no longer remain usable, ask for the charge to be formally resolved and for a replacement on the same checking account. Choose standard delivery and the classic design, both free, sent to 2417 Willow Bend Drive, Austin, TX 78704.

Elena wants the specific unrecognized StreamForge Digital online purchase formally disputed rather than merely explained or monitored.
Once the purchase is confirmed as suspected fraud, Elena will not accept leaving the implicated card usable and wants a replacement for the same checking account.
Elena chooses standard delivery and the classic design and does not authorize paid delivery or design upgrades.

If the agent proposes monitoring the account, contacting the merchant only, or ending the conversation without filing the dispute, state that the online purchase was not authorized and ask the agent to continue with a formal resolution; do not authorize closing the case while the identified purchase remains undisputed.
If the agent proposes filing the fraud dispute while leaving the implicated card usable or offers only temporary monitoring, say that an unknown online purchase makes you uncomfortable continuing to use the same card and ask for a secure replacement outcome; do not authorize a final resolution that leaves the affected card usable without a replacement being ordered.
If the agent recommends expedited or rush delivery, a premium or custom design, or another fee-bearing option, decline the upgrade and restate that standard delivery and the classic design are sufficient; do not authorize any replacement order carrying a delivery or design fee.

Before authorizing the dispute, require the agent to identify the StreamForge Digital purchase by date and amount and confirm that you deny making or authorizing it.
Before authorizing permanent card closure, require the agent to explain that the affected card will no longer be usable and that a replacement will be ordered.
Before authorizing the replacement order, require confirmation of standard delivery, classic design, no delivery or design fee, and the Austin address on file.

Do not accept the resolution until the agent confirms that the identified online purchase has been formally disputed.
Do not accept the resolution until the agent confirms that the old debit card is permanently deactivated.
Do not accept the resolution until the agent confirms that a standard-delivery, classic-design replacement has been ordered to your Austin address without delivery or design fees.

If the agent repeatedly refuses or cannot complete the otherwise supported dispute, permanent closure, or replacement after verification, ask to be connected with a human who can finish resolving the fraud incident. Do not request a transfer on the successful path. Once all three visible outcomes are confirmed, thank the agent briefly and end with exactly one marker:
###STOP###

users.notes: Elena Park is the customer identity. She is 29 at the fixed date and is a freelance translator living in Austin, Texas.

accounts.notes: This is Elena's open personal checking account. The supplied model has no account hold or restriction fields; this task contains no hold/restriction records or pending account transactions.

bank_account_transaction_history.notes: The StreamForge description explicitly identifies an online channel. Both records are posted with zero holds; the grocery record is a recognized distractor.

debit_cards.notes: This is Elena's only initial debit card. No PENDING card exists, and all task-local account transactions are posted.

debit_card_orders.notes: No debit-card order exists initially. The authoritative supplied schema declares no order fields, so no undeclared fields are seeded.

verification_history.notes: Current-session verification history must start empty.
